paper_definition.text: line 476 bundles depreciation, maintenance, insurance and driver wages and says the cost is proportional to dispatched delivery trips; lines 478-479 define F2=c_fix*sum n_kp z_kp.

implementation.text: Physical vehicle IDs are de-duplicated for n_veh metrics at lines 164-165, but line 168 charges len(solution.routes)*vehicle_fixed_cost; profit allocation also adds the price once per route.

value_provenance_conflict.finding: The 170-yuan proxy is derived from monthly rental and acquisition-equivalent values divided by paid days. Lines 39 and 51 explicitly assume one model shift per vehicle per day. That provenance is vehicle-day/shift based, not evidence that depreciation/rent should be recharged for every trip when one physical vehicle performs multiple same-day trips.

current_resetp_audit.specific_conflict: paper_main.tex:476 says depreciation, maintenance, insurance and wages are proportional to the number of delivery trips, and paper_main.tex:1034 calls 170 yuan a per-trip dispatch fee, while the source derivation in china_cost_proxy_evidence_20260718.md:30-31 and 39-51 is monthly vehicle rent/acquisition equivalent allocated once per paid vehicle-day under the hidden one-shift-per-day assumption. cost.py:168 then repeats that daily vehicle proxy for every route of the same physical vehicle.
current_resetp_audit.one_sentence_conclusion: In the explicit entity-multitrip sample, the mainstream unit is each used physical vehicle (or no monetary fixed cost when fleet size is exogenous), not each trip; ReSETP's current per-trip charging is therefore not self-consistent with an entity-vehicle multitrip interpretation of the same 170-yuan vehicle-day proxy.
